subproblem.title: Linear algebra of tilted cones: points violating the L-graph inequality over P lie, with a ball around them, in the cone around T^⊥
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, 0 < L ≤ 1 and P, T ∈ G(N,n), with p := Grassmannian.project P and p_T := Grassmannian.project T, such that ‖p_T u − p u‖ ≤ (L/4)‖u‖ for all u ∈ ℝ^N. If v, w ∈ ℝ^N satisfy L‖p v‖ < ‖v − p v‖ and ‖w − v‖ ≤ (L/8)‖v‖, then (L/16)‖w‖ ≤ ‖w − p_T w‖ and ‖w‖ ≤ 2‖v‖.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (P T : Grassmannian N n) (v w : Euclidean N), 0 < L → L ≤ 1 → (∀ u : Euclidean N, ‖Grassmannian.project T u - Grassmannian.project P u‖ ≤ L / 4 * ‖u‖) → L * ‖Grassmannian.project P v‖ < ‖v - Grassmannian.project P v‖ → ‖w - v‖ ≤ L / 8 * ‖v‖ → L / 16 * ‖w‖ ≤ ‖w - Grassmannian.project T w‖ ∧ ‖w‖ ≤ 2 * ‖v‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3, (3.1) and (3.2), of the parent proof with c = L/4 and γ = L/8. The first conclusion is the inequality |q_T w| ≥ (c/4)|w| = (L/16)|w| established inside (3.2); by Pythagoras it says w ∈ K_α(T) = {|p_T w| ≤ α|w|} with α = (1 − L²/256)^{1/2}. Notation: for S ∈ G(N,n), p_S := Grassmannian.project S and q_S(u) := u − p_S u; p := p_P, q := q_P.

0. Projection facts. For S ∈ G(N,n), p_S is linear, symmetric (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric: ⟨p_S a, b⟩ = ⟨a, p_S b⟩) and idempotent (Grassmannian.project_project). Hence for every u: ⟨p_S u, u − p_S u⟩ = ⟨p_S u, u⟩ − ⟨p_S u, p_S u⟩ = ⟨p_S u, u⟩ − ⟨u, p_S(p_S u)⟩ = ⟨p_S u, u⟩ − ⟨u, p_S u⟩ = 0, so Pythagoras (norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_real for p_S u + (u − p_S u) = u) gives ‖u‖² = ‖p_S u‖² + ‖q_S u‖². In particular ‖q_S u‖ ≤ ‖u‖. Also q_S is linear: q_S(a + b) = q_S a + q_S b. (These are proved inline; no extra named lemma is needed.)

1. |q v| > (L/2)|v|. Put a := ‖q v‖ and b := ‖p v‖, so ‖v‖² = b² + a², and by hypothesis a > L b ≥ 0. Squaring nonnegative quantities, a² > L²b² = L²(‖v‖² − a²). Since L ≤ 1, L²a² ≤ a², hence L²‖v‖² = L²b² + L²a² < a² + a² = 2a². Then (2a)² = 4a² > 2L²‖v‖² ≥ (L‖v‖)², and as 2a ≥ 0 and L‖v‖ ≥ 0 we get 2a > L‖v‖, i.e. a > (L/2)‖v‖.

2. |q_T v| > (L/4)|v|. q_T v − q v = p v − p_T v, so ‖q_T v − q v‖ = ‖p_T v − p v‖ ≤ (L/4)‖v‖ (tilt hypothesis with u = v). By the reverse triangle inequality (norm_sub_norm_le), ‖q_T v‖ ≥ ‖q v‖ − ‖q v − q_T v‖ > (L/2)‖v‖ − (L/4)‖v‖ = (L/4)‖v‖.

3. ‖w‖ ≤ 2‖v‖. ‖w‖ ≤ ‖v‖ + ‖w − v‖ ≤ (1 + L/8)‖v‖ ≤ 2‖v‖, using L ≤ 1 and ‖v‖ ≥ 0. This is the second conclusion.

4. (L/16)‖w‖ ≤ ‖q_T w‖. By linearity, q_T w = q_T v + q_T(w − v), and by step 0, ‖q_T(w − v)‖ ≤ ‖w − v‖ ≤ (L/8)‖v‖. Hence ‖q_T w‖ ≥ ‖q_T v‖ − ‖q_T(w − v)‖ > (L/4)‖v‖ − (L/8)‖v‖ = (L/8)‖v‖ ≥ (L/16)‖w‖, the last step by step 3 and L > 0. As q_T w = w − p_T w, this is the first conclusion. ∎
proof_key_steps: Symmetric idempotent projections satisfy Pythagoras ‖u‖² = ‖p_S u‖² + ‖u − p_S u‖², so ‖u − p_S u‖ ≤ ‖u‖.
L‖p v‖ < ‖q v‖ and L ≤ 1 give ‖q v‖ > (L/2)‖v‖.
The tilt bound ‖p_T − p‖ ≤ L/4 gives ‖q_T v‖ > (L/4)‖v‖.

The successive L/2, L/4, and L/8 estimates correctly yield both the L/16 cone inequality and the factor-2 norm bound. subproblem.title: H^n of a centred closed ball in an n-plane equals ω_n r^n
subproblem.statement: For N, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ G(N,n) and r ≥ 0: μHE[n](T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n, i.e. H^n(T ∩ B_r(0)) = ω_n r^n, where ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (T : Grassmannian N n) (r : ℝ), 0 ≤ r → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ((T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)) ∩ closedBall 0 r) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal r ^ n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step (1.2) of the parent proof (normalisation), stated for every r ≥ 0. Notation: W := T.plane, a linear subspace of ℝ^N; ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); H := μHE[n] (on ℝ^N and on ℝ^n).

1. finrank W = n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane). Hence W, with the inner product induced from ℝ^N, has an orthonormal basis b indexed by Fin n: take Mathlib's stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ W (indexed by Fin (finrank ℝ W)) and reindex it along finCongr (Grassmannian.finrank_plane T) : Fin (finrank ℝ W) ≃ Fin n.

2. Let J : ℝ^n → ℝ^N be the composition of b.repr.symm : ℝ^n ≃ₗᵢ W with the inclusion W.subtypeₗᵢ : W →ₗᵢ ℝ^N. J is a linear isometry, in particular an isometry of metric spaces, and its range is W.

3. J(closedBall(0, r)) = W ∩ closedBall(0, r). (⊆) For u ∈ ℝ^n with ‖u‖ ≤ r: J u ∈ W, and ‖J u‖ = ‖b.repr.symm u‖ = ‖u‖ ≤ r (the norm of an element of W is its norm in ℝ^N, Submodule.norm_coe; b.repr.symm preserves norms, LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map). (⊇) For y ∈ W with ‖y‖ ≤ r put u := b.repr y; then ‖u‖ = ‖y‖ ≤ r and J u = y.

4. By isometry invariance of the Euclidean Hausdorff measure (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), H(J(closedBall(0, r))) = μHE[n](closedBall(0, r)) computed in ℝ^n, and on ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) we have μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).

5. volume is an additive Haar measure on ℝ^n and finrank ℝ^n = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so for r ≥ 0, Measure.addHaar_closedBall gives volume(closedBall(0, r)) = ofReal(r^n) · volume(ball(0, 1)) = ofReal(r^n) · unitBallVolume n (definition of unitBallVolume). As r ≥ 0, ofReal(r^n) = ofReal(r)^n (ENNReal.ofReal_pow).

6. Combining steps 3–5: H(W ∩ closedBall(0, r)) = ofReal(r)^n · unitBallVolume n = unitBallVolume n · ofReal(r)^n. ∎ (No case distinction is needed; e.g. for n = 0 this reads H^0({0}) = 1 = ω_0, and for r = 0, n ≥ 1 it gives H^n({0}) = 0.)

Formalization note (checked in a scratch copy): b := (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T.plane).reindex (finCongr T.finrank_plane); J := T.plane.subtypeₗᵢ.comp b.repr.symm.toLinearIsometry; then rw [← himg, J.isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Measure.addHaar_closedBall _ _ hr, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, unitBallVolume, ENNReal.ofReal_pow hr, mul_comm].
proof_key_steps: An orthonormal basis of T.plane indexed by Fin n (finrank_plane) gives a linear isometry J : ℝ^n → ℝ^N with range T.plane.
J(closedBall 0 r) = T.plane ∩ closedBall 0 r.
Isometry invariance of μHE[n] and μHE[n] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n).
addHaar_closedBall: volume(closedBall 0 r) = ofReal(r^n)·volume(ball 0 1) = ω_n·ofReal(r)^n.

audit.reason: The orthonormal-basis isometry identifies the plane ball exactly. Isometry invariance, normalized Hausdorff measure on Euclidean n-space, and the Haar closed-ball formula prove the frozen equality, including r = 0 and n = 0. No additional dimension hypothesis is needed.

subproblem.title: Weight blow-ups at a tangent point converge to θ·H^n on the tangent plane (Def. 8.1.1 tested with functions of position only)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U (Varifold N n U), x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ (Simon Ch. 8, Def. 1.1). Then for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ): t^{−n} ∫ g(t^{−1}(y − x)) dμ_V(y) → θ ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n as t ↓ 0 (t > 0), where μ_V = V.weight and H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → ∀ g : C_c(Euclidean N, ℝ), Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ t⁻¹ ^ n * ∫ y, g (t⁻¹ • (y - x)) ∂V.weight) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ * ∫ y in (T.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), g y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step (1.1) of the parent proof (the cone/Lipschitz-graph argument of Simon's printed proof of Ch. 3, Thm 1.6 '⇐', run at varifold tangent points in the sense of Ch. 8, Def. 1.1), with every identification written out. Notation: μ := V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst; G := Grassmannian N n; H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N; W := (T.plane : Set ℝ^N); for t > 0, φ_t : ℝ^N × G → ℝ^N × G, φ_t(z) := (t^{−1}·(z.1 − x), z.2), so rescaledMeasure V x t = ofReal(t^{−1}^n) • V.measure.map φ_t (definition); ι : ℝ^N → ℝ^N × G, ι(y) := (y, T), so planeVarifoldMeasure T = (H.restrict W).map ι (definition).

1. The lifted test function. Fix g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) and define f : ℝ^N × G → ℝ by f(y, S) := g(y). f = g ∘ Prod.fst is continuous. Let K := tsupport g ×ˢ univ. K is compact: tsupport g is compact because g has compact support, and G is a compact space (SimonGMT instance Grassmannian.instCompactSpace), so K = tsupport g × G is compact (IsCompact.prod with isCompact_univ). If z ∉ K then z.1 ∉ tsupport g, hence f(z) = g(z.1) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). By HasCompactSupport.intro, f has compact support, i.e. f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G, ℝ).

2. Applying Def. 1.1. The third conjunct of HasTangentPlane V x T θ, applied to f, gives
 ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) → θ · ∫ f d(planeVarifoldMeasure T) as t → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0.

3. The limit. ι is measurable (measurable_id.prodMk measurable_const) and f is continuous, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for every measure. By the change-of-variables formula for push-forward measures (integral_map),
 ∫ f d((H.restrict W).map ι) = ∫ f(ι(y)) d(H.restrict W)(y) = ∫ g(y) d(H.restrict W)(y) = ∫_{W} g dH.
 So the limit in step 2 is θ ∫_W g dH.

4. The blow-up integrals for t > 0. Let t > 0. (a) integral_smul_measure: ∫ f d(c • ν) = c.toReal · ∫ f dν for c ∈ [0,∞]; here c = ofReal(t^{−1}^n) and c.toReal = t^{−1}^n because t^{−1}^n ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). (b) φ_t is continuous, hence measurable, so integral_map gives ∫ f d(V.measure.map φ_t) = ∫ f(φ_t z) dV.measure(z) = ∫ g(t^{−1}·(z.1 − x)) dV.measure(z). (c) Prod.fst is measurable and y ↦ g(t^{−1}·(y − x)) is continuous, so integral_map gives ∫ g(t^{−1}·(z.1 − x)) dV.measure(z) = ∫ g(t^{−1}·(y − x)) d(V.measure.map Prod.fst)(y) = ∫ g(t^{−1}·(y − x)) dμ(y). Hence for every t > 0:
 ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) = t^{−1}^n · ∫ g(t^{−1}·(y − x)) dμ(y).
 No integrability is needed: integral_map and integral_smul_measure are identities of Bochner integrals, valid whether or not the integrands are integrable.

5. Conclusion. The functions t ↦ ∫ f d(rescaledMeasure V x t) and t ↦ t^{−1}^n ∫ g(t^{−1}(y − x)) dμ(y) agree on (0, ∞), and (0, ∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). By Tendsto.congr', steps 2–4 give t^{−1}^n ∫ g(t^{−1}·(y − x)) dμ(y) → θ ∫_W g dH as t → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0, which is the claim. ∎

Formalization note (checked in a scratch copy importing GMT.Ch08.Submission): build f as ⟨⟨fun z ↦ g z.1, g.continuous.comp continuous_fst⟩, HasCompactSupport.intro (g.hasCompactSupport.prod isCompact_univ) _⟩; rewrite with integral_map (f := fun z ↦ f z) using Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable of map_continuous f; then filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin], unfold rescaledMeasure, rw [integral_smul_measure, integral_map, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal], and finish with integral_map along measurable_fst.
proof_key_steps: Lift g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) to f(y,S) := g(y); f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) because G is compact (f vanishes off tsupport g × G).
Apply the third conjunct of HasTangentPlane V x T θ to f.
Identify the limit: integral_map along y ↦ (y,T) turns θ∫ f dv(T) into θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n.
For t > 0 identify the blow-up integral: integral_smul_measure (toReal(ofReal t^{−n}) = t^{−n}) and integral_map along φ_t and along Prod.fst give t^{−n}∫ g(t^{−1}(y − x)) dμ_V.
Transfer the limit with Tendsto.congr' on (0,∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0.

subproblem.title: Cone decay at a tangent point (n ≥ 1): the mass near x in a cone around T^⊥ is o(t^n)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U, x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n) and θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ, and let β > 0; write p_T := Grassmannian.project T. Then for every ε ∈ (0,∞] there is δ > 0 such that for all t ∈ (0,δ): μ_V({y ∈ B_t(x) : β|y − x| ≤ |(y − x) − p_T(y − x)|}) ≤ ε t^n (B_t(x) = closedBall x t).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), 0 < n → HasTangentPlane V x T θ → ∀ β : ℝ, 0 < β → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), V.weight {y | y ∈ closedBall x t ∧ β * ‖y - x‖ ≤ ‖(y - x) - Grassmannian.project T (y - x)‖} ≤ ε * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step (1.4) of the parent proof (cone decay). The parent's cone K_α(T) = {v : |p_T v| ≤ α|v|}, α ∈ (0,1), equals {v : β|v| ≤ |v − p_T v|} with β = (1 − α²)^{1/2}, by Pythagoras |v|² = |p_T v|² + |v − p_T v|²; the argument below is that of (1.4), works for every β > 0 and does not need this identification. Uses the siblings weight_blowup (Submission.tgc_weight_blowup_tendsto) and plane_ball_measure (Submission.tgc_plane_closedBall_hausdorff). Notation: μ := V.weight; H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N; W := (T.plane : Set ℝ^N); ν := H.restrict W; p := Grassmannian.project T (linear, hence continuous since ℝ^N is finite-dimensional: LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional applied to projectionLinearMap); for t > 0, S_t := {y : y ∈ closedBall(x,t) ∧ β‖y − x‖ ≤ ‖(y − x) − p(y − x)‖} (the set in the statement).

1. The case ε = ∞. For t > 0, ofReal(t)^n ≠ 0, so ∞ · ofReal(t)^n = ∞ and the bound is trivial on (0,∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0. Assume ε < ∞ and put e := ε.toReal > 0. HasTangentPlane gives x ∈ U and θ > 0.

2. The set C. Let C := {w : ‖w‖ ≤ 1 ∧ β‖w‖ ≤ ‖w − p w‖}. C is closed (intersection of sets {f ≤ g} with f, g continuous: isClosed_le), C ⊆ closedBall(0,1), and 0 ∈ C (p 0 = 0). Scaling: if t > 0 and y ∈ S_t then w := t^{−1}·(y − x) ∈ C, because ‖w‖ = ‖y − x‖/t ≤ 1 and, by linearity of p, w − p w = t^{−1}·((y − x) − p(y − x)), so β‖w‖ = t^{−1}β‖y − x‖ ≤ t^{−1}‖(y − x) − p(y − x)‖ = ‖w − p w‖.

3. C meets the plane in a null set. If w ∈ C ∩ W then p w = w (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_apply_of_mem: the projection fixes its range W), so β‖w‖ ≤ ‖w − p w‖ = 0 and ‖w‖ = 0 (β > 0). Thus C ∩ W ⊆ W ∩ closedBall(0,0), and plane_ball_measure with r = 0 gives H(W ∩ closedBall(0,0)) = ω_n · ofReal(0)^n = 0 because n ≥ 1. Hence ν(C) = H(C ∩ W) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply, C closed hence measurable; measure_mono_null).

4. Thickenings; choice of κ. For 0 ≤ r ≤ 1, cthickening r C ⊆ cthickening r (closedBall(0,1)) = closedBall(0, r + 1) ⊆ closedBall(0,2) (cthickening_subset_of_subset, cthickening_closedBall). By plane_ball_measure with r = 2, ν(closedBall(0,2)) = ω_n·ofReal(2)^n < ∞ (ω_n < ∞ by measure_ball_lt_top), so ν(cthickening 1 C) < ∞. Since C is closed, tendsto_measure_cthickening_of_isClosed gives ν(cthickening r C) → ν(C) = 0 as r → 0. Hence eventually in 𝓝 0, ν(cthickening r C) < ofReal(e/θ); taking δ from Metric.eventually_nhds_iff and κ := min(δ/2, 1), we get 0 < κ ≤ 1 and ν(cthickening κ C) < ofReal(e/θ); in particular ν(cthickening κ C) < ∞ and ν(cthickening κ C).toReal < e/θ.

5. A cut-off. Define g(v) := max(0, 1 − infDist(v, C)/κ). g is continuous (continuous_infDist_pt), 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, and g = 1 on C (infDist_zero_of_mem). If v ∉ cthickening κ C then infDist(v, C) ≥ κ: otherwise, as C is nonempty (0 ∈ C), infDist_lt_iff gives w ∈ C with dist(v, w) < κ, and then v ∈ cthickening κ C (mem_cthickening_of_dist_le) — a contradiction; so 1 − infDist(v, C)/κ ≤ 0 and g(v) = 0. Hence g vanishes outside cthickening κ C ⊆ closedBall(0,2), a compact set, and g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ).

6. The limit is < e. 0 ≤ g ≤ 1_{cthickening κ C} pointwise, and this indicator is ν-integrable (the set is closed, ν of it is finite). By integral_mono_of_nonneg and integral_indicator_const, ∫_W g dH = ∫ g dν ≤ ν(cthickening κ C).toReal < e/θ, so ℓ := θ ∫_W g dH < θ · (e/θ) = e. By weight_blowup, F(t) := t^{−1}^n ∫ g(t^{−1}·(y − x)) dμ(y) → ℓ, so eventually in 𝓝[>] 0, F(t) < e.

7. Finite mass near x. U is open (V.isOpen_domain) and x ∈ U, so there is R > 0 with ball(x,R) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff); closedBall(x,R/2) ⊆ ball(x,R) ⊆ U is compact, so μ(closedBall(x,R/2)) < ∞ (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact). Eventually in 𝓝[>] 0 also t ≤ R/4 (Ioc_mem_nhdsGT).

8. Fix t with 0 < t ≤ R/4 and F(t) < e (an 𝓝[>] 0-eventual set by steps 6–7), and put h_t(y) := g(t^{−1}·(y − x)).
 (a) h_t vanishes outside closedBall(x, R/2): if h_t(y) ≠ 0 then t^{−1}(y − x) ∈ cthickening κ C ⊆ closedBall(0,2), so ‖y − x‖ ≤ 2t ≤ R/2.
 (b) h_t is μ-integrable: it is continuous and bounded by 1 on closedBall(x,R/2), a set of finite μ-measure (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded), and zero outside it (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset).
 (c) 1_{S_t} ≤ ofReal ∘ h_t pointwise: for y ∈ S_t, t^{−1}(y − x) ∈ C by step 2, so h_t(y) = 1. S_t is closed (closedBall ∩ {continuous ≤ continuous}), hence measurable, so μ(S_t) = ∫⁻ 1_{S_t} dμ ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(h_t) dμ = ofReal(∫ h_t dμ) (lintegral_indicator_one, lintegral_mono, ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal using (b) and h_t ≥ 0).

9. Conclusion. ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · μ(S_t) ≤ ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · ofReal(∫ h_t dμ) = ofReal(F(t)) ≤ ofReal(e) = ε (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). Multiplying by ofReal(t)^n and using ofReal(t)^n · ofReal(t^{−1}^n) = 1 for t > 0: μ(S_t) = ofReal(t)^n · (ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · μ(S_t)) ≤ ofReal(t)^n · ε = ε · ofReal(t)^n. This holds on an 𝓝[>] 0-eventual set, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: ε = ∞ is trivial; otherwise e := ε.toReal > 0.
C := {‖w‖ ≤ 1, β‖w‖ ≤ ‖w − p_T w‖} is closed, bounded, contains 0, and t^{−1}(S_t − x) ⊆ C.
C ∩ T.plane ⊆ {0}, which is H^n-null for n ≥ 1 (plane_ball_measure with r = 0).
ν := H^n⌞T.plane: ν(cthickening κ C) → ν(C) = 0 (tendsto_measure_cthickening_of_isClosed, finite via plane_ball_measure r = 2); pick κ ∈ (0,1] with θ ν(C_κ) < e.
Cut-off g = max(0, 1 − infDist(·,C)/κ) ∈ C_c, 1_C ≤ g ≤ 1_{C_κ}; by weight_blowup the blow-up integrals tend to θ∫ g dν < e.
For small t the rescaled cut-off is μ_V-integrable (support in a compact ball inside U) and μ_V(S_t) ≤ ∫ g((y − x)/t) dμ_V < e t^n.

subproblem.title: Abstract cone/density covering lemma: points with a lower mass bound and cone decay lie on countably many closed L-Lipschitz graphs over P
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, 0 < L ≤ 1, μ any measure on ℝ^N, P ∈ G(N,n) with p := Grassmannian.project P, and A ⊆ ℝ^N. Suppose every x ∈ A admits T ∈ G(N,n) with ‖p_T v − p v‖ ≤ (L/4)‖v‖ for all v (p_T := Grassmannian.project T) such that (i) there is c ∈ (0,∞] with c t^n ≤ μ(B_t(x)) for all sufficiently small t > 0, and (ii) for every ε ∈ (0,∞], μ({y ∈ B_t(x) : (L/16)|y − x| ≤ |(y − x) − p_T(y − x)|}) ≤ ε t^n for all sufficiently small t > 0. Then there are closed sets Γ_0, Γ_1, … ⊆ ℝ^N with ‖(y − z) − p(y − z)‖ ≤ L‖p(y − z)‖ for all y, z ∈ Γ_i (L-Lipschitz graphs over P) such that every x ∈ A lies in some Γ_i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) (P : Grassmannian N n) (A : Set (Euclidean N)), 0 < L → L ≤ 1 → (∀ x ∈ A, ∃ T : Grassmannian N n, (∀ v : Euclidean N, ‖Grassmannian.project T v - Grassmannian.project P v‖ ≤ L / 4 * ‖v‖) ∧ (∃ c : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n ≤ μ (closedBall x t)) ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μ {y | y ∈ closedBall x t ∧ L / 16 * ‖y - x‖ ≤ ‖(y - x) - Grassmannian.project T (y - x)‖} ≤ ε * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n) → ∃ Γ : ℕ → Set (Euclidean N), (∀ i, IsClosed (Γ i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ y ∈ Γ i, ∀ z ∈ Γ i, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖) ∧ ∀ x ∈ A, ∃ i, x ∈ Γ i
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–6 of the parent proof — uniform classes replacing Egoroff (printed (7)–(9)), the graph claim (printed (10)) and the closed graph pieces — for an abstract measure. The varifold enters the parent proof only through the lower mass bound (1.3) and the cone decay (1.4); here these are hypotheses (i) and (ii), and the parent's constant (2m)^{−1}ω_n is replaced by a_m := 1/m (ω_n is absorbed into c). Uses the sibling cone_linear_algebra (Submission.tgc_tilted_cone_inclusion). Notation: p := Grassmannian.project P, q(v) := v − p v; for T ∈ G(N,n), p_T := Grassmannian.project T; Tilt(T) :⟺ ∀ v, ‖p_T v − p v‖ ≤ (L/4)‖v‖; for x ∈ ℝ^N and t > 0, K(T,x,t) := {y : y ∈ closedBall(x,t) ∧ (L/16)‖y − x‖ ≤ ‖(y − x) − p_T(y − x)‖}; 'the graph inequality for (y,z)' means ‖q(y − z)‖ ≤ L‖p(y − z)‖. Only monotonicity of μ is used (no finiteness or measurability).

1. Constants. γ := L/8 ∈ (0, 1/8]. For integers m ≥ 1: a_m := 1/m > 0 and ε_m := a_m (γ/2)^n / 2 > 0. For every s ≥ 0, ε_m (2s)^n = a_m (γ/2)^n 2^n s^n / 2 = a_m (γs)^n / 2.

2. Uniform classes. For integers m, k ≥ 1 let E_{m,k} be the set of x ∈ ℝ^N for which there is T ∈ G(N,n) with Tilt(T) such that for every t ∈ (0, 1/k]:
 (i') ofReal(a_m t^n) ≤ μ(closedBall(x,t)), and (ii') μ(K(T,x,t)) ≤ ofReal(ε_m t^n).

3. The classes cover A. Let x ∈ A and take T, c from the hypothesis. As c ≠ 0, ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt gives m ∈ ℕ with (m : [0,∞])^{−1} < c; necessarily m ≥ 1 (for m = 0 the left side is ∞), and ofReal(a_m) = m^{−1} < c. Apply (ii) with ε := ofReal(ε_m) > 0. Both (i) and this instance of (ii) hold eventually in 𝓝[>] 0, so by Metric.mem_nhdsWithin_iff there is δ > 0 such that for all t ∈ (0,δ): c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(closedBall(x,t)) and μ(K(T,x,t)) ≤ ofReal(ε_m) · ofReal(t)^n. Choose an integer k ≥ 1 with 1/k < δ (exists_nat_gt applied to 1/δ). For t ∈ (0, 1/k] we have t < δ, so ofReal(a_m t^n) = ofReal(a_m) · ofReal(t)^n ≤ c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(closedBall(x,t)) and μ(K(T,x,t)) ≤ ofReal(ε_m) · ofReal(t)^n = ofReal(ε_m t^n) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, t ≥ 0). Hence x ∈ E_{m,k} with witness T.

4. Graph property inside a class (printed (10)). CLAIM: if x, x' ∈ E_{m,k} and ‖x' − x‖ ≤ 1/(2k), then ‖q(x' − x)‖ ≤ L‖p(x' − x)‖. Suppose not, and put v := x' − x, so L‖p v‖ < ‖q v‖. Then v ≠ 0 (for v = 0 both sides vanish since p 0 = 0), so s := ‖v‖ satisfies 0 < s ≤ 1/(2k). Let T witness x ∈ E_{m,k}; at x' only (i') is used, so the witness for x' plays no role.
 (a) closedBall(x', γs) ⊆ K(T, x, 2s): for y with ‖y − x'‖ ≤ γs put w := y − x. Then w − v = y − x', so ‖w − v‖ ≤ (L/8)‖v‖, and cone_linear_algebra (applied to L, P, T, v, w with Tilt(T) and L‖p v‖ < ‖v − p v‖) gives (L/16)‖w‖ ≤ ‖w − p_T w‖ and ‖w‖ ≤ 2‖v‖ = 2s; that is, y ∈ closedBall(x, 2s) and y satisfies the cone inequality, so y ∈ K(T, x, 2s).
 (b) Since 0 < γs ≤ 2s ≤ 1/k (γ ≤ 1/8 < 2 and s ≤ 1/(2k)), (i') at x' with t = γs, monotonicity of μ with (a), and (ii') at x with t = 2s give
  ofReal(a_m (γs)^n) ≤ μ(closedBall(x', γs)) ≤ μ(K(T, x, 2s)) ≤ ofReal(ε_m (2s)^n).
 (c) As ε_m (2s)^n ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff turns (b) into a_m (γs)^n ≤ ε_m (2s)^n = a_m (γs)^n / 2 (step 1), contradicting a_m (γs)^n > 0. This proves the claim.

5. Closed pieces. Let (d_j)_{j∈ℕ} be a dense sequence in ℝ^N (ℝ^N is separable and nonempty: TopologicalSpace.denseSeq with denseRange_denseSeq). For m, k ≥ 1 and j ∈ ℕ put S_{m,k,j} := E_{m,k} ∩ closedBall(d_j, 1/(4k)) and Γ_{m,k,j} := closure(S_{m,k,j}).
 (a) Γ_{m,k,j} is closed (isClosed_closure).
 (b) Graph inequality on Γ_{m,k,j}: for y, z ∈ S_{m,k,j}, ‖y − z‖ ≤ ‖y − d_j‖ + ‖z − d_j‖ ≤ 1/(4k) + 1/(4k) = 1/(2k), so step 4 with x := z, x' := y gives ‖q(y − z)‖ ≤ L‖p(y − z)‖. The set F := {(y,z) ∈ ℝ^N × ℝ^N : ‖q(y − z)‖ ≤ L‖p(y − z)‖} is closed (isClosed_le of two continuous functions; p is continuous as a linear map on a finite-dimensional space), and S × S ⊆ F for S := S_{m,k,j}. Hence closure(S) × closure(S) = closure(S × S) ⊆ F (closure_prod_eq, closure_minimal): the graph inequality holds for all y, z ∈ Γ_{m,k,j}.
 (c) Covering: if x ∈ E_{m,k}, density gives j with dist(x, d_j) < 1/(4k) (DenseRange.exists_dist_lt), so x ∈ S_{m,k,j} ⊆ Γ_{m,k,j} (subset_closure).

6. Enumeration. Let π : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ × ℕ, π(i) := (i.unpair.1, i.unpair.2.unpair.1, i.unpair.2.unpair.2); π(Nat.pair a (Nat.pair b c)) = (a, b, c) (Nat.unpair_pair), so π is surjective. Define Γ_i := Γ_{a+1, b+1, c} where π(i) = (a, b, c). Each Γ_i is closed and satisfies the graph inequality for all its pairs of points (step 5(a),(b)). If x ∈ A, step 3 gives m, k ≥ 1 with x ∈ E_{m,k}, step 5(c) gives j with x ∈ Γ_{m,k,j}, and i := Nat.pair (m − 1) (Nat.pair (k − 1) j) satisfies Γ_i = Γ_{m,k,j} ∋ x. This proves the statement. ∎ (Lean note: it is convenient to index the classes directly by m, k ∈ ℕ with a := 1/(m+1) and radii 1/(k+1); the argument is unchanged.)

Uniform classes E_{m,k} (lower bound a_m t^n and cone bound ε_m t^n for all t ∈ (0,1/k]) cover A, using hypotheses (i), (ii) and 𝓝[>] 0.

Closures of E_{m,k} ∩ closedBall(d_j, 1/(4k)), d_j dense, are closed L-graphs over P (closed condition) covering E_{m,k}.
Enumerate the triples (m,k,j) by Nat.unpair.

subproblem.title: Lower mass bound at a tangent point: liminf t^{−n} μ_V(B_t(x)) ≥ θ ω_n (eventual form)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N, V an n-varifold on U, x ∈ ℝ^N, T ∈ G(N,n), θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ. Then for every c ∈ [0,∞] with c < ofReal(θ) · ω_n (ω_n = unitBallVolume n) there is δ > 0 such that c · t^n ≤ μ_V(B_t(x)) for all t ∈ (0, δ); i.e. ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] 0, c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ V.weight (closedBall x t).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, c < ENNReal.ofReal θ * unitBallVolume n → ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), c * ENNReal.ofReal t ^ n ≤ V.weight (closedBall x t)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step (1.3) of the parent proof, in 'eventually' form. Uses the sibling results weight_blowup (Submission.tgc_weight_blowup_tendsto) and plane_ball_measure (Submission.tgc_plane_closedBall_hausdorff). Notation: μ := V.weight; ω := unitBallVolume n; H := μHE[n] on ℝ^N; W := (T.plane : Set ℝ^N); ν := H.restrict W.

1. Finiteness; real numbers. HasTangentPlane V x T θ gives θ > 0. ω = volume(ball(0,1)) in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is finite (measure_ball_lt_top), so a := ofReal θ · ω < ∞, and c < a forces c < ∞. Put c_r := c.toReal and a_r := θ · ω.toReal = a.toReal (ENNReal.toReal_mul, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal). Since c, a < ∞ and c < a, c_r < a_r (ENNReal.toReal_lt_toReal).

2. Choice of κ. The map κ ↦ a_r κ^n is continuous and equals a_r at κ = 1; hence it tends to a_r > c_r as κ → 1 from the left, so eventually in 𝓝[<] 1 we have c_r < a_r κ^n, and eventually κ ∈ (0,1) (Ioo_mem_nhdsLT). Choose κ with 0 < κ < 1 and c_r < a_r κ^n.

3. A cut-off. Define g(v) := min(1, max(0, (1 − ‖v‖)/(1 − κ))) for v ∈ ℝ^N. g is continuous, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1; if ‖v‖ ≤ κ then (1 − ‖v‖)/(1 − κ) ≥ 1, so g(v) = 1; if ‖v‖ ≥ 1 then (1 − ‖v‖)/(1 − κ) ≤ 0, so g(v) = 0. Thus g vanishes outside the compact set closedBall(0,1) and g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) (HasCompactSupport.intro).

4. Lower bound for the limit value. By plane_ball_measure with r = 1, ν(closedBall(0,1)) = H(W ∩ closedBall(0,1)) = ω < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply and commutativity of ∩). As g is continuous, |g| ≤ 1 and g = 0 off closedBall(0,1), g is ν-integrable (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded on closedBall(0,1), then integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset). Pointwise 1_{closedBall(0,κ)} ≤ g (g ≥ 0 everywhere, g = 1 on closedBall(0,κ)), and the indicator is ν-integrable because ν(closedBall(0,κ)) = ω · ofReal(κ)^n < ∞ (plane_ball_measure with r = κ ≥ 0). By monotonicity of the integral (integral_mono) and integral_indicator_const:
 ∫_W g dH = ∫ g dν ≥ ν(closedBall(0,κ)).toReal = (ω · ofReal(κ)^n).toReal = ω.toReal · κ^n.
 Multiplying by θ > 0: ℓ := θ ∫_W g dH ≥ a_r κ^n > c_r.

5. Eventually large blow-up integrals. By weight_blowup applied to g, F(t) := t^{−1}^n ∫ g(t^{−1}·(y − x)) dμ(y) → ℓ as t → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0. As ℓ > c_r, eventually F(t) > c_r (Tendsto.eventually with eventually_gt_nhds); also eventually t > 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). Fix such a t; it remains to show c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ μ(closedBall(x,t)).

6. Comparison with the ball mass. If μ(closedBall(x,t)) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise put h_t(y) := g(t^{−1}·(y − x)). Then 0 ≤ h_t ≤ 1_{closedBall(x,t)}: if y ∉ closedBall(x,t) then ‖t^{−1}(y − x)‖ = ‖y − x‖/t > 1, so h_t(y) = 0; and h_t ≤ 1 everywhere. The indicator is μ-integrable since μ(closedBall(x,t)) < ∞, so by integral_mono_of_nonneg, ∫ h_t dμ ≤ ∫ 1_{closedBall(x,t)} dμ = μ(closedBall(x,t)).toReal. Hence c_r < F(t) ≤ t^{−1}^n · μ(closedBall(x,t)).toReal.

7. Back to [0,∞]. Since c < ∞ and μ(closedBall(x,t)) < ∞: c = ofReal(c_r) and ofReal(t^{−1}^n · μ(closedBall(x,t)).toReal) = ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · μ(closedBall(x,t)) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with t^{−1}^n ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). As c_r ≥ 0, the strict real inequality of step 6 gives c < ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · μ(closedBall(x,t)) (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff_of_nonneg). Multiplying by ofReal(t)^n and using ofReal(t)^n · ofReal(t^{−1}^n) = ofReal((t·t^{−1})^n) = 1 for t > 0:
 c · ofReal(t)^n ≤ ofReal(t^{−1}^n) · μ(closedBall(x,t)) · ofReal(t)^n = μ(closedBall(x,t)).
 This holds on an 𝓝[>] 0-eventual set of t, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: θ > 0 and ω_n < ∞, so c < θω_n is finite; pick κ ∈ (0,1) with c < θ ω_n κ^n (continuity of κ ↦ κ^n at 1).
θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n ≥ θ H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0)) = θ ω_n κ^n > c (plane_ball_measure).
weight_blowup: t^{−n}∫ g((y − x)/t) dμ_V → θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n, hence eventually > c.
t^{−n}∫ g((y − x)/t) dμ_V ≤ t^{−n} μ_V(B_t(x)); multiply back by t^n in [0,∞].

subproblem.title: For n = 0 the tangent points of a varifold are atoms of μ_V, hence countable
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N and V a 0-varifold on U (Varifold N 0 U). Then the set {x ∈ ℝ^N : HasTangentPlane V x T θ for some T ∈ G(N,0) and θ ∈ ℝ} is countable.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N 0 U), {x : Euclidean N | ∃ (T : Grassmannian N 0) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ}.Countable
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (degenerate dimension n = 0): every tangent point is an atom of the σ-finite weight measure, and a σ-finite measure has at most countably many atoms. Uses the sibling lower_mass_bound (Submission.tgc_tangent_weight_lower_bound) with n = 0. Notation: μ := V.weight.

1. Atoms are countable. μ is σ-finite (instance Varifold.weight.instSigmaFinite), hence s-finite. The singletons {y}, y ∈ ℝ^N, are measurable (measurableSet_singleton) and pairwise disjoint (Set.disjoint_singleton), so by Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion the set A₀ := {y : 0 < μ({y})} is countable. It suffices to prove that every x in the set of the statement satisfies μ({x}) > 0: then that set is contained in A₀ and is countable (Set.Countable.mono).

2. A positive lower bound near x. Let HasTangentPlane V x T θ. Then x ∈ U and θ > 0. ω_0 := unitBallVolume 0 = volume(ball(0,1)) in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 0) is positive (Metric.measure_ball_pos: volume is an additive Haar measure, so it charges nonempty open sets). So a := ofReal θ · ω_0 > 0 (ENNReal.mul_pos), and there is c with 0 < c < a (exists_between in [0,∞]). By lower_mass_bound with n = 0: eventually as t → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0, c · ofReal(t)^0 ≤ μ(closedBall(x,t)); since ofReal(t)^0 = 1, this says c ≤ μ(closedBall(x,t)).

3. Finite mass near x. U is open (V.isOpen_domain) and x ∈ U, so there is R > 0 with ball(x,R) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff). closedBall(x,R/2) ⊆ ball(x,R) is compact and contained in U, so μ(closedBall(x,R/2)) < ∞ (Varifold.weight_finite_on_compact).

4. Continuity from above. Let s_j := closedBall(x, (R/2)/(j+1)) for j ∈ ℕ. The s_j are closed (so measurable), decreasing in j, μ(s_0) < ∞ by step 3, and ⋂_j s_j = {x} (x lies in every s_j; if y ≠ x choose j with (R/2)/(j+1) < dist(y,x), possible since (R/2)/(j+1) → 0). By tendsto_measure_iInter_atTop, μ(s_j) → μ(⋂_j s_j) = μ({x}). The radii (R/2)/(j+1) are positive and tend to 0 (tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat), so they tend to 0 within (0,∞), i.e. in 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff); by step 2, c ≤ μ(s_j) for all sufficiently large j. Passing to the limit (ge_of_tendsto), c ≤ μ({x}), so μ({x}) ≥ c > 0.

5. By steps 1 and 4 the set of tangent points is contained in the countable set A₀, hence is countable. ∎
proof_key_steps: The atoms {y : 0 < μ_V{y}} of the σ-finite weight are countable (countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion).
lower_mass_bound with n = 0 and 0 < c < θ ω_0 gives c ≤ μ_V(B_t(x)) for small t > 0.
x ∈ U gives finite mass of a small closed ball; continuity from above along B_{R/(2(j+1))}(x) ↓ {x} yields μ_V({x}) ≥ c > 0.
So every tangent point is an atom; the set of tangent points is countable.

audit.reason: The n = 0 lower bound gives positive mass on sufficiently small balls. Local finiteness at the tangent point permits continuity from above to a positive singleton mass; sigma-finiteness then makes the set of such atoms countable. This proves exactly the stated set-countability obligation without using the covering theorem.
